chunks: Zur‘ah narrated from Samā‘ah, who said:

I asked him about a man who died and left sons and daughters, young and old, without any bequest, and he had servants, slaves, and jewelry. How should the heirs divide that inheritance? He said: "If a trustworthy man undertakes the division of all that among them, then there is no harm."

key_terms.الْمِيرَاثِ: the inherited estate or property left behind
key_terms.الْوَرَثَةُ: the legal heirs entitled to inherit
key_terms.عُقَدٌ: jewelry or tied valuables within the estate
key_terms.قَاسَمَهُمْ: he apportioned or divided it among them
key_terms.مَمَالِيكُ: owned slaves belonging to the estate
key_terms.وَصِيَّةٍ: a bequest or will left by the deceased

ai.seo_question: Can a trustworthy person divide an inheritance when the deceased left no will?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the division of an estate when a deceased person leaves heirs but no will. It indicates that there is no harm in a trustworthy man carrying out the division of the inheritance among the heirs, including when the estate contains varied property and some heirs are minors.
